is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles funestus, the principal malaria vector in Eastern and Southern Africa (page 2, line 29).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports Vgsc L976F (L1014F in An. gambiae) and P1842S (P1874S in An. gambiae) (page 7, lines 148-151; Table 1, page 8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 2A (page 10) provides allele frequencies for multiple regions and years, and the text mentions 333 samples were analyzed (page 4, line 107).

african_field_population.evidence: The study analyzes Anopheles funestus samples collected from ten administrative regions in Tanzania (page 15, lines 306-308).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting the discovery of kdr mutations in An. funestus based on whole-genome sequencing of 333 samples (page 2, lines 32-33).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data for ten administrative regions in Tanzania: Dodoma, Kagera, Katavi, Lindi, Morogoro, Mtwara, Mwanza, Pwani, Ruvuma, and Tanga (page 15, lines 306-308).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports data for specific collection years (e.g., 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023) (page 10, Figure 2A).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper states the samples were collected as part of a countrywide Anopheles funestus surveillance project in Tanzania and incorporated into the MalariaGEN Anopheles funestus genomic surveillance project database (page 15, lines 309-311). This is a standard reporting of a large-scale surveillance project, not a duplicate of a previously published paper.

supplement.evidence: The necessary data, including sample numbers and primer sequences, are provided in the main text and supplementary tables included in the PDF.

assessment.summary: This study reports the first discovery of kdr mutations (L976F and P1842S) in Anopheles funestus in Tanzania. The study used whole-genome sequencing of 333 mosquitoes collected across ten regions between 2017 and 2023. The mutations were found in tight linkage disequilibrium and were associated with DDT resistance, but not deltamethrin resistance.
